newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador official disputes $3 bln telecom valuation.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador official disputes $3 bln telecom valuation.

text.p: The valuation of Ecuador's state telecommunications firm Emetel at $3 billion by the former government of President Abdala Bucaram is arbitrary, a top government official said Monday.

"The previous government arbitrarily put the figure at $3 billion, which has nothing to do with the assets, nor with the replacement cost, nor with revenues," Raul Gangotena, director of the government's National Modernization Council, told Reuters in an interview.
Gangotena said that a new valuation for Emetel would be ready by September, but that the firm was worth about $800 million at the end of 1995, and about $1.2 billion computing replacement costs.
U.S. firms MCI and GTE, Italy's Stet, Spain's Telefonica de Espana and Korea Telecom have all signed up to bid for 35 percent of Emetel in a privatization due in November.
Bucaram was deposed by Congress on grounds of "mental incompetence" after only six months in office two months ago.
